{"path": "vqa_visualization.py", "content": """"
VQA Benchmark Accuracy Visualization
Visualizes vision-language model performance across different question types.
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# VQA Accuracy Data by Question Type
data = {
    'Yes/No': {
        'CLIP': 82.1,
        'BLIP-2': 87.4,
        'LLaVA': 89.2,
        'GPT-4V': 92.3
    },
    'Number': {
        'CLIP': 43.2,
        'BLIP-2': 51.7,
        'LLaVA': 56.3,
        'GPT-4V': 63.8
    },
    'Other': {
        'CLIP': 51.4,
        'BLIP-2': 58.2,
        'LLaVA': 63.1,
        'GPT-4V': 70.5
    }
}

# Model colors
model_colors = {
    'CLIP': '#1f77b4',
    'BLIP-2': '#ff7f0e',
    'LLaVA': '#2ca02c',
    'GPT-4V': '#d62728'
}

# Set up the figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Position for each group of bars
x = np.arange(len(data.keys()))  # Question type positions
width = 0.2  # Width of each bar

# Create grouped bar chart
for i, (model, color) in enumerate(model_colors.items()):
    values = [data[qt][model] for qt in data.keys()]
    bars = ax.bar(x + i * width, values, width, label=model, color=color, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.2)
    
    # Add value labels on top of each bar
    for bar in bars:
        height = bar.get_height()
        ax.annotate(f'{height}%',
                    xy=(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, height),
                    xytext=(0, 3),
                    textcoords="offset points",
                    ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

# Customize the chart
ax.set_xlabel('Question Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Accuracy (%)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Vision-Language Model Performance on VQA Benchmark\nby Question Type', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xticks(x + width * 1.5)
ax.set_xticklabels(['Yes/No', 'Number', 'Other'], fontsize=12)
ax.legend(title='Model', title_fontsize=11, fontsize=10, loc='upper left')
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)

# Add annotation highlighting that Number questions are hardest
ax.annotate('Number questions are hardest for ALL models',
            xy=(0.5, 0.05),
            xycoords='axes fraction',
            fontsize=12, fontweight='bold',
            ha='center',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.8))

# Add annotation about GPT-4V's lead on Number questions
number_gpt4v_lead = 63.8 - 56.3  # GPT-4V vs LLaVA (second best)
ax.annotate(f'GPT-4V leads by {number_gpt4v_lead:.1f}% on Number questions',
            xy=(0.5, 0.01),
            xycoords='axes fraction',
            fontsize=11,
            ha='center',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightblue', alpha=0.8))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('vqa_accuracy_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.show()

print("Visualization saved to vqa_accuracy_chart.png")"}

messages.content:
"""
VQA Benchmark Accuracy Visualization
Visualizes vision-language model performance across different question types.
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# VQA Accuracy Data by Question Type
data = {
    'Yes/No': {
        'CLIP': 82.1,
        'BLIP-2': 87.4,
        'LLaVA': 89.2,
        'GPT-4V': 92.3
    },
    'Number': {
        'CLIP': 43.2,
        'BLIP-2': 51.7,
        'LLaVA': 56.3,
        'GPT-4V': 63.8
    },
    'Other': {
        'CLIP': 51.4,
        'BLIP-2': 58.2,
        'LLaVA': 63.1,
        'GPT-4V': 70.5
    }
}

# Model colors (lighter, warmer pink, purple, blue, yellow)
model_colors = {
    'CLIP': '#ffc0cb',
    'BLIP-2': '#e6e6fa',
    'LLaVA': '#b0e0e6',
    'GPT-4V': '#fffacd'
}

# Set up the figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Position for each group of bars
x = np.arange(len(data.keys()))  # Question type positions
width = 0.2  # Width of each bar

# Create grouped bar chart
for i, (model, color) in enumerate(model_colors.items()):
    values = [data[qt][model] for qt in data.keys()]
    bars = ax.bar(x + i * width, values, width, label=model, color=color, edgecolor='none')
    
    # Add value labels on top of each bar
    for bar in bars:
        height = bar.get_height()
        ax.annotate(f'{height}%',
                    xy=(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, height),
                    xytext=(0, 5),
                    textcoords="offset points",
                    ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Customize the chart
ax.set_xlabel('Question Type', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Accuracy (%)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Vision-Language Model Performance on VQA Benchmark\nby Question Type', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xticks(x + width * 1.5)
ax.set_xticklabels(['Yes/No', 'Number', 'Other'], fontsize=14)
ax.legend(title='Model', title_fontsize=13, fontsize=12, loc='upper right')
ax.tick_params(axis='y', which='major', labelsize=14, width=2, length=6)
ax.set_yticks([40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90])
ax.set_ylim(40, 100)



plt.tight_layout()
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_visible(False)
plt.savefig('vqa_accuracy_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.show()

print("Visualization saved to vqa_accuracy_chart.png")

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

function.name: find
function.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

function.name: ls
function.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)
